page: Microsoft Azure D96_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and driven by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. It delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical processor cores with two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 384.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction flags include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, paired with 48 MB of L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent top-quartile multi-core compute and memory throughput. The instance achieves strong scores in multi-threaded benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (17,166.0), multi-core stress-ng (93,238.58), and PassMark CPU score (76,687.04). Hardware-accelerated cryptographic processing is a distinct strength, reaching top-decile performance on PassMark encryption tests. Large-block memory bandwidth is substantial, registering 325.48 GB/sec on uncached reads and 140.05 GB/sec on writes. Conversely, single-threaded metrics such as Geekbench single-core and gzip compression rank within the middle 50th percentile, reflecting the 2.8 GHz baseline operating frequency.

The D96_v5 configuration includes no local NVMe storage and provides zero bundled public IPv4 addresses, requiring all persistent and scratch storage to be mounted via remote networked volumes. Resource allocation offers high core density without the cost overhead of dedicated GPU accelerators. This architecture is well structured for scaled enterprise workloads, including large database deployments, high-throughput static web serving, Clang compilation jobs, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines.

It features 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, alongside hardware extensions such as AVX-512 and SHA-NI. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks show upper-quartile multi-threaded compute, high memory throughput, and top-decile cryptographic acceleration, though single-core performance remains mid-tier. This configuration is tailored for large-scale enterprise workloads such as database systems, Redis instances, CI/CD build environments, and parallel batch processing.
